newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber steady to firm on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber steady to firm on shortcovering.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady to firm on Wednesday on modest shortcovering by Japanese houses looking to buy their monthly requirements for RSS1 rubber, dealers said.
"There was some buying from Japanese houses this afternoon engaged in a bit of shortcovering. But the other months were dull and trading was very thin," a local rubber trader said.

Some 1,700 tonnes of forward purchases were made by Japanese buyers taking advantage of low prices in the local exchange, the traders said. Volume for RSS3 rubber, on the other hand, reached just a little over 500 tonnes, the dealers said.
"Some of the buyers were holding back though on expectations that prices will still drift lower over the next few days," another rubber trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 123.00-124.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.00 cents.
July/September RSS1 was seen steady at 186.00 Singapore cents (US$1.33) a kg.
February TSR20 was seen at 172.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg from 172.25 cents.
